about: Knowledge Graph spec D §4.1 quality fixture: 60 items, 6 labels x (7 tickets + 3 notes). A ticket's text is its title, its description and its comments, folded as the pipeline folds them. Hand-written 2026-10-03; never generated.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Ticket sheet jumps to the top on phone. Scrolling the details sheet on an iPhone snaps back to the header whenever the keyboard closes. Comment: same on Android Chrome after editing the title.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Bottom sheet cannot be dragged down to close. On small screens the grab handle is covered by the safe-area inset, so swiping down does nothing.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Keyboard hides the comment box on mobile. Typing a comment in the sheet, the on-screen keyboard covers the input and the view does not scroll it into sight.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Momentum scroll stops halfway in the phone sheet. A flick inside the sheet stops dead when it reaches the subtasks list; the inner list steals the touch.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Tap targets in the sheet header are too small. The close and more buttons are 24 px on phones; people hit the title instead. Comment: make them 44 px.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Rubber-band overscroll drags the whole page behind the sheet. Pulling past the end of the sheet bounces the board underneath on iOS Safari.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Landscape phone: sheet is taller than the viewport. Rotating the phone leaves the sheet's footer off screen with no way to scroll to Save.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Phone pass rulings. The sheet owns its own scroll container; the page never scrolls under it. Touch gestures inside lists are contained with overscroll-behavior. Inputs scroll into view above the keyboard.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Mobile sheet test checklist: open on a 390 px screen, scroll to the bottom, open the keyboard, rotate, swipe to dismiss, and check the header buttons with a thumb.

items.label: phone-sheet
items.text: Why the sheet scroll resets: re-rendering the sheet on every keystroke remounts the scroll container and its scrollTop goes back to zero on small screens.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Card jumps back after dropping it in another column. Dragging a card from To do to Doing shows it in Doing for a moment, then it snaps back to its old column.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Drop indicator appears in the wrong slot. When dragging between two cards the blue line shows one position lower than where the card lands.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Dragging a card is laggy on a board with 300 cards. The card trails the pointer by half a second; every move re-renders all columns. Comment: memoise the column list.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Reordering inside a column loses the rank. Moving a card to the top of Doing and reloading puts it back in the middle; the new rank key was never saved.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Cannot drop a card into an empty column. Empty columns have no drop target, so a card can only go into columns that already hold cards.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Auto-scroll while dragging near the board edge. Dragging a card to a column off screen should scroll the board sideways; today it stops at the edge.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Blocked transition is not explained when a drop is refused. Dropping a card on Done when the workflow forbids it bounces the card back with no message.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Board drag and drop design: a dragged card is a ghost under the pointer; columns highlight as drop targets; a refused move returns the card and names the rule that refused it.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Rank keys between cards: dropping between two cards takes a key between their keys, so moving one card never rewrites the order of the others in the column.

items.label: board-drag
items.text: Optimistic moves on the board: the card moves at once, the transition is sent, and on a refusal the card animates back to the column it came from.

items.label: search
items.text: Search does not find a ticket by a word in its description. Typing compressor finds titles but misses tickets that only mention it in the body.

items.label: search
items.text: Misspelt queries return nothing. Searching for 'refridgerator' should suggest refrigerator instead of an empty result list.

items.label: search
items.text: Meaning search ranks an unrelated note first. Asking for 'cold storage problems' returns a note about invoices above the freezer log. Comment: check the embedding model.

items.label: search
items.text: Search snippet shows the wrong part of the note. The highlighted excerpt is from the first paragraph even when the match is near the end.

items.label: search
items.text: Searching by ticket key after a prefix change. Old keys like CS-12 should still find the ticket that is now GN-12.

items.label: search
items.text: Index new notes faster. A freshly saved note does not appear in results for ten seconds; the indexer only runs on its interval.

items.label: search
items.text: Search results ignore the project filter. Choosing one project still lists hits from every project in the workspace.

items.label: search
items.text: How search works: lexical matching with prefixes and typo correction for words, and a meaning mode that compares embedded chunks of each note with the query.

items.label: search
items.text: Search ranking notes: title matches outrank body matches; a ticket key match comes first; results are cut at fifty with no paging.

items.label: search
items.text: Embedding model choice: a static model with one vector per token, mean pooled, chosen because the ONNX runtime would not load on the alpine image.

items.label: trash
items.text: Deleted ticket still shows on the board. After deleting a ticket from its sheet the card stays on the board until a reload.

items.label: trash
items.text: Restore puts the ticket back without its subtasks. Restoring a deleted parent from the trash leaves its children deleted.

items.label: trash
items.text: Purge after fifteen days did not run. Items deleted three weeks ago are still listed in the trash; the nightly purge sweep skipped them. Comment: the sweep log shows a timeout.

items.label: trash
items.text: Mark for purge should ask for confirmation. Marking a project for permanent deletion happens on one click with no warning about what is erased.

items.label: trash
items.text: Trash list does not say who deleted an item. Show the person and the time beside each deleted ticket, note and project.

items.label: trash
items.text: Undelete a workspace from the trash. An owner who deletes a workspace by mistake has no way to bring it back within the fifteen days.

items.label: trash
items.text: Erased ticket keys are reused. After a purge the next new ticket took the number of the erased one; numbers must never be reused.

items.label: trash
items.text: Trash and purge rules: delete moves an item to the trash, restore brings it back, and fifteen days later the purge erases it permanently, keeping only a redacted record.

items.label: trash
items.text: What a purge erases: the item's rows in every table, its attachments in storage, its search index and chunks, and its events are redacted in place.

items.label: trash
items.text: Archive versus delete: archiving a project hides it from live lists but keeps everything; deleting starts the fifteen day clock toward permanent erasure.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Mention notifications arrive twice. Being @mentioned in a comment sends one email and then a second identical email a minute later.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Bell badge count does not clear after reading. Opening the notifications panel marks items read but the red unread count stays at 3. Comment: needs a refetch.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Daily email digest instead of one email per change. People asked for a single morning summary of everything assigned to them.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Mute notifications for one project. A member on five projects wants alerts from only two of them.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Assignment email links to the wrong workspace. Clicking the link in the you-were-assigned email opens the first workspace instead of the ticket's.

items.label: notifications
items.text: No notification when a ticket I watch is closed. Collaborators should hear about closing and reopening, not only the assignee.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Unsubscribe link in emails does nothing. The footer link opens a blank page and the person keeps receiving alerts.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Notification kinds: assigned, mentioned, due soon, overdue, closed. Each can be muted per person; the bell shows unread ones and email follows the same rules.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Email delivery setup: the sender domain, the bounce handling, and why alerts are batched for five minutes before an email goes out.

items.label: notifications
items.text: Who gets told what: the assignee and collaborators of a ticket, anyone mentioned in its text, and nobody for their own actions.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Passkey sign-in fails on a new laptop. Registering a passkey works but signing in with it on the second device says credential not found.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: OTP text message arrives after the code has expired. The SMS with the six digit code takes three minutes and the code is valid for two. Comment: extend to five.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Magic link email opens a signed-out page. Clicking the sign-in link from the email on a phone lands on the login screen again.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Session expires while writing a long comment. After an hour the next save fails with unauthorised and the typed text is lost.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Sign out of every device. A person who lost a phone needs to end all their sessions and revoke its passkey from settings.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Device login code for the MCP connector. The assistant shows a short code to approve on the website; approving it does not finish the login.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Too many wrong codes should lock the number for a while. Repeated failed OTP attempts are not rate limited.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Sign-in methods: a phone number with a one-time code, an email magic link, and passkeys once a person has signed in once on that device.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Session rules: sessions last thirty days and refresh on use; signing out ends this device only; a revoked passkey cannot start a new session.

items.label: sign-in
items.text: Authentication audit: codes are hashed at rest, attempts are counted per number, and every sign-in records the device and time.
